seoDescription: Learn the fundamentals of structuring a Django project by creating your first application. This tutorial explains the concept of a 'Django app' as a modular component of your website, responsible for a single piece of functionality. You'll see how to start and stop the Django development server using `manage.py runserver`, understand why it auto-reloads on code changes, and learn the command-line workflow for managing your project. Finally, you'll use `manage.py startapp` to generate the boilerplate files for a new app.

chapters.title: Running the Development Server
chapters.description: Learn how to start, stop, and manage the Django development server using the command line and PyCharm.

chapters.description: The instructor demonstrates how to keep the development server running in a separate terminal to allow for other command-line work.

chapters.title: Explaining Django Apps
chapters.description: The instructor clarifies what an app is in the context of a Django project after a brief rant about the overuse of the term.

chapters.title: The Single Responsibility Principle for Apps
chapters.description: Understand the core design rule that each Django app should do one thing and be describable in a single sentence.

chapters.title: Brainstorming an App-Based Project
chapters.description: An example of a peer-to-peer file-sharing program is used to illustrate how a complex project is broken down into multiple Django apps.

chapters.description: Follow the step-by-step process of using the `python manage.py startapp` command to generate a new app in your Django project.

summary:
## Running the Development Server
- **Start the server**: Use the command `python manage.py runserver` in your project's root directory.
- **Stop the server**: Press `Ctrl+C` in the terminal where the server is running.
- **Auto-reloading**: The Django development server automatically detects changes to your source code and reloads, so you don't need to manually restart it during development.

> [!TIP]
> It's common practice to keep the server running in one terminal window and open a separate terminal for running other management commands.

## Understanding Django Apps
- A Django project is composed of multiple **apps**.
- An **app** is a self-contained, modular component that handles one specific piece of your website's functionality.
- **Examples**: A forum, a video player, or a user profile system could each be implemented as a separate app within a single Django project.

### The Single Responsibility Principle
- **Core Rule**: Each app should do only one thing.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> If you cannot describe what your app does in a single, simple sentence, it is a strong indicator that you should break it into smaller, more focused apps.

## Creating a New App
- To create a new app, navigate to your project's root directory (the one containing `manage.py`).
- Use the `startapp` management command followed by the desired name for your app.
- **Command Syntax**:
  ```
  python manage.py startapp <app_name>
  ```
- **Example**:
  ```
  python manage.py startapp music
  ```
- This command generates a new directory for the app (e.g., `music/`) containing a standard set of boilerplate files to get you started.

So again, in Django you have a website, your main project, and it's composed of all these little apps. Now, it's actually pretty cool how Django works with apps because they help you organize all the different parts of your website. Now another random thing I want to talk to you guys about before we get started is this: way back when, I actually had a pretty cool idea for a program.
